text:
The Nifty 50 closed around 25,530, just below its daily pivot (P 25562.03) and the 200‑day moving average (DMA 23997.45), marking a modest pull‑back after four weeks of gains. The move was broad‑based: most sectors participated, with the leading quadrant (PSU banks, realty, banks, financial services, consumption, auto, FMCG) holding up better than the lagging ones (IT, energy, PSU stocks, metal).  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers in index futures, holding 34.1 % long positions but reducing net contracts by 70,454 (down 2,207 contracts from the prior session). This outflow added pressure on the market. Options data showed 149 short signals as Nifty fell 451 points, indicating bearish positioning. Sector‑wise, banks and financials faced the heaviest selling, while MNC‑driven stocks showed some improvement.  

Watch the next session for Nifty’s support at S1 25,131.47 and resistance at R1 25,780.22; a break below S1 could test the 200‑day average. In Bank Nifty, key levels are S1 61,689.9 and R1 64,337.1. Keep an eye on global cues – especially AI‑related news from Nvidia – and any domestic policy updates that could affect rupee carry flows or margin‑trading activity. (Jargon: “pivot” is the mid‑point of the day’s range; “short signals” are option bets expecting a fall.)
